topic_map.authoring: Classical ideal gas at thermal equilibrium; mean random translational kinetic energy in the gas rest frame, not bulk-flow or total molecular energy.
One mole, molar volume, number density and Avogadro naming retained; original molar-number notation and equation3-11 reference unchanged.
Equation3-12 preserved; macroscopic pressure/volume linked to mean molecular center-of-mass translational energy, excluding internal and interaction energies.
Empirical one-mole ideal-gas equation3-13 and section17 reference preserved; temperature explicitly absolute and expressed in kelvin, not Celsius.
Same equilibrium gas used when equating the two right-hand sides; equation3-14 unchanged.
Absolute-temperature proportionality retained; faster is a statistical mean-square-speed statement for the same gas, not identical individual or cross-species speeds.

Liquids, solids and gas/wall comparison retained with classical equipartition and comparable kinetic-degree conditions; liquids not universally lattice-bound. Total energy distinguished from kinetic energy; zero-temperature trend identified as classical extrapolation.
Footnote marker and low-temperature quantum qualification retained; minimum-energy state does not imply all motion stops, and bound quantum particles may retain zero-point motion.
